external_basis.citation: Dugger et al. 2026, Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 14:1868960
external_basis.published_rule: 239 birds at Cape Crozier and Cape Royds were coded unavailable during 2016-2018 while wearing geolocator tags on their legs to account for possible device effects on survival or detection.

frozen_resolution_hierarchy.preferred: If, before full behavioral-row access, an authoritative public source provides the 239 Band IDs and tagged seasons, reproduce the published individual-season censoring exactly.
fallback_if_ids_not_recoverable: Exclude all first-breeding choice events with first_breeding_season in 2016, 2017, or 2018 from the primary analysis.
Treat banded-breeder performance years 2016, 2017, and 2018 as unavailable unless tagged breeder-seasons can be removed using an authoritative ID list.
Do not infer that an unmarked resight row was untagged merely because Notes or other free-text fields lack a geolocator mention.

interaction_with_other_gates.bird_rule: The independent BIRD post-2013 candidate-set exclusion remains unchanged.
interaction_with_other_gates.information_gate: Apply geolocator censoring before counting source-level and multi-candidate events for the frozen 100/50 thresholds.
interaction_with_other_gates.performance_gate: A missing/censored performance year removes the entire first-breeding event when that prior year is required; do not substitute a different lookback year.

claim_boundary: Do not identify tagged individuals from behavioral outcome patterns.
Do not use free-text Notes to construct a post hoc tagged subset after outcomes are opened unless a parsing rule is frozen from external documentation first.
Do not drop this censoring because it reduces sample size.
This is a design-protection rule, not evidence that geolocators materially affected the birds in this dataset.
